statement: The admitted production HTTP profile program validates exactly the independently specified 23 scalar fields and three relations, preserves accepted scalar values in a defensive copy, and determines a unique valid abstract empty Admission state from that copy, a Boolean lane and an explicit signed integer clock sample.

scope.allRequiredConsumers: Exactly the registered initialization consumers and the import/re-export bindings they use; this is not a source-wide service configuration inventory.

positive_seconds.floatEncoding: Exact positive-denominator as_integer_ratio; reject NaN and both infinities; preserve integer versus floating representation.

defaultConsequences.qualification: Burst 64 and rate 32 describe the default pair only. The admitted custom-profile domain does not impose those combined burst/rate caps.

normalization.profileType: Exact TrafficProfile type identity; subclasses and arbitrary duck-typed objects are rejected.
normalization.defaultSentinel: Only an explicitly registered None default at a constructor boundary may select the specified default profile; no general truthiness fallback.
normalization.snapshot: Read each registered field into a fresh exact TrafficProfile, validate all copied fields and relations, and preserve their accepted scalar values. No original profile container alias is retained as the admitted configuration.
normalization.invalidValues: Reject through a registered constant ValueError diagnostic without rendering the invalid input or invoking its user-defined numeric methods.
normalization.allocationOrder: Normalize configuration and validate the lane and sampled clock before creating Admission locks, buckets and registries or binding a listener socket. This does not assert validation before all enclosing Portal resources.

clockSample.role: Explicit external origin sample, not a configurable duration or a claim of future clock monotonicity.

validity: anonymousOwners is empty and every anonymous owner is in owners
peers is empty and cardinality(peers) <= profile.peer_entries
last = supplied clock sample; no sign restriction on the clock origin
initialization.uniqueness: For fixed profile scalar values, Boolean lane and signed clock sample, exactly one abstract state satisfies the independent initialization relation. Concrete object/lock identity is erased by the declared abstraction.
initialization.ownershipAbstraction: The initially empty concrete set, list and OrderedDict map to the corresponding empty abstract collections. This does not prove future reserve/release transitions, lock atomicity, container allocation bytes or ownership of socket/OS resources.
initialization.constructorLinkage: The closed AST mapping must connect the real Admission and TokenBucket initial assignments to the pure initialization result, account for every relevant assigned field and reject overrides or bypasses; detached pure-function correctness is insufficient.

runtimeBoundary: Reject profile subclasses, attribute-bearing impostors and falsey non-None impostors.
Reject an exact TrafficProfile whose fields were made invalid before normalization; mutating the original after normalization must not mutate the copy.
Reject non-Boolean lane values including 0, 1 and truthy objects before runtime allocation.
Reject Boolean, fractional, nonfinite, subclass and object clock samples; accept negative and arbitrarily large exact integers.
Observe one clock sample per Admission initialization and exact initial public/control fields, zero counters and empty ownership/peer collections.
Demonstrate invalid profile/lane/sample rejection before the registered lock, bucket, registry and listener allocation points.
mutationControls: Added, removed, duplicate, miswired or misclassified profile fields must block the bridge or independent acceptance proof.
An altered line/header, header-count or combined-handler relation must fail its independent relational theorem or boundary witness.
A wrong lane selector, token unit, initial credit, counter, ownership collection or constructor assignment must fail the independent initial-state theorem or linkage verifier.
Removed defensive copy, truthiness fallback, weakened exact type checks, unexpected code or module rebinding must fail the closed AST verifier.
An introduced axiom and a placeholder proof must each fail the registered proof gate.

verificationContract.theoremAudit: Audit every project theorem including generated and private declarations and each complete transitive axiom set; do not exclude failing generated declarations.
prohibited: proof of a fixed known-good formula substituted for extracted production guards
verificationContract.independence: This schema and its relational/initial semantics are authored independently of extraction. Generated production Lean must not generate the expected schema or specification from its own implementation.
verificationContract.evidenceBinding: Before a closure run, register exact theorem types, witnesses, verifiers and production mappings; hash the full source/specification/proof/verifier/test/dependency inputs and bind all raw evidence to the same closure ID and canonical input root.
verificationContract.determinism: Compare theorem inventory, generated correspondence and provenance metadata, claim-status set and registered reproducible artifact hashes across the two builds.
verificationContract.reviews: Two GPT-6 Luna, then two GPT-6.1 Sol, then two GPT-6 Astra source-bound adversarial reviews; mechanically checked breaches can block, while review text is never proof evidence.
blockOn: failed theorem or nonempty axiom audit
verificationContract.designQualification: This specification fixes a candidate surface and reports no execution result. A later registered verifier report is required for closure.

components: Pinned Lean kernel, compiler and installed distribution
Frozen restricted AST translator, constructor/import linkage checker, theorem audit, witness checker, closure verifier and input hashing
Exact built-in type identity, integer arithmetic, scalar comparisons and int/float.as_integer_ratio
Dataclass construction, ordinary attribute access, immutable built-in scalar copying and registered standard-library empty-container semantics
No monkey-patched built-ins/imports, hostile concurrent mutation during normalization or executable rebinding outside the admitted source
Successful clock callback supplies its explicit validated sample without hostile mutation or reentrancy
Successful ordinary lock/container construction has the registered initial interpretation; concrete allocation identities are erased
The theorem describes successful initialization, not resource exhaustion, arbitrary asynchronous interruption or OS socket behavior
Linux isolation, filesystem/process semantics and execution hardware

excluded: Complete TRF-00 or any complete original TRF obligation
Complete service/deployment byte, age, RSS, process, cache, evidence, snapshot, queue and channel profile
Independent analysis observation schema, diagnostic/disclosure semantics and behavioral-instance equivalence
Whole Portal initialization, random generations and service identities, OS handles, socket binding, locks/threads/process execution or enclosing constructor rollback
Future Admission reserve/release/refill histories, rate conservation, nonborrowability under concurrency, decoder behavior and resource allocation bytes
Shared-host budgets, proxy/IIS/CDN buffering, platform containment, runtime latency and warm-worker history independence
Arbitrary Python code, hostile trusted code, later source revisions and undeclared deployment environments
